name: Colin Lopez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel, and your answers are confidential. What is an ordinary day at your accounting firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58, an experienced accountant with a bachelor’s degree and a professional accountancy qualification, preparing accounts and tax returns for small garages. I like finding the repair order that explains a strange parts total, but chasing the same missing invoice wears me out. Elise and I have grown children, and lower pay plus barely two weeks saved makes retirement a question, not a date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small AI gain is close to what I see now when garage invoices arrive. I use AI every day to group parts and labour questions, but I still check the actual repair order.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the desk that speed is useful only when the parts total is right. A garage owner should be able to see why a tax figure changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, my pay is low for an experienced accountant and we have barely two weeks of costs saved. My partner Elise works at a bakery, and few similar firms are nearby, so the ordinary bills already keep me tense.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned garage accounts and returns and take the duplicate-parts errors I catch to our staff association meeting. I would ask the manager for paid time to check the AI suggestions rather than having us do it after hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious even in this mild world because one missed wage would empty the small reserve. The tool is not the thing that keeps me up; the rent date is.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which correction did you make recently?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The AI sorter doubled a garage’s starter motor because the repair order repeated it. I called before filing; the owner had copied an old estimate by mistake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What could the association change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The association can ask for paid checking time, but it cannot make the bakery wage cover our rent. I would keep a written count of corrected parts every month.

say: I would ask that **parts totals** be shown to garage clients.
I would press for **paid checking time** instead of evening work.
think: My **lower pay** and two week reserve already make a missed wage serious.
Few nearby firms mean a **job gap** would be hard to close.
do: Keep preparing **assigned garage returns** and checking daily AI suggestions against repair orders.
Take a **monthly duplicate-parts count** to the staff association for paid checking time.
feel: **Anxious** about rent and a tiny reserve before new disruption.
S0.quote: The AI sorter doubled a garage’s starter motor because the repair order repeated it.
fieldNote: His **starter-motor correction** shows a daily AI user who still phones the garage when a parts total looks wrong.
The **two week reserve**, low pay and few nearby firms explain anxiety even when AI stays a small helper.

steps.text: Keep assigned garage returns checked against repair orders and daily AI suggestions
Bring monthly duplicate-parts count to association for paid checking time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Stronger software could write and check the returns that fill my week, so my experience would not keep every hour paid. The robots come later, but our records are already on screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the association for a written rule on paid review hours and who signs a machine-prepared return. I would tell clients to ask for the corrected parts list.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my own paid hours may fall when the firm sells a faster return. Elise’s bakery wage cannot meet the rent alone, and two weeks saved leaves us little room to test that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask manager Ruth for paid supervised time on the new parts-audit screen using six closed garage files, and learn it if approved. If she refuses, I will check assigned paid files with the current tool while offered and work through free examples at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a possible cut in my own week. I can learn a screen quickly, but I cannot learn my way out of unpaid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do after a cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my hours actually fall, I will apply for posted utility billing roles only with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start and shifts that fit Elise’s bakery mornings. A recruiter call is not enough.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the new screen safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use the new screen live only after Ruth signs a report showing it found all six planted errors without exposing client records. I would bring those results to the association before accepting a higher target.

say: I would seek **paid review rules** and named sign off through the association.
I would show clients the **corrected parts list**.
think: My own **paid hours** may fall with cheaper automated returns.
Elise’s wage and **two weeks saved** cannot cover our rent gap.
do: Learn the **new parts-audit screen** on six closed garage files in Ruth-approved paid supervision.
If hours fall, seek **posted utility billing** with written rent-and-food-covering pay, confirmed start and Elise-compatible shifts; keep paid files while offered.
Use the **live screen** only after Ruth signs that it found all six planted errors without exposing client records.
feel: **Anxious** about a possible cut to my paid week.
S1.quote: I can learn a screen quickly, but I cannot learn my way out of unpaid hours.
fieldNote: The **new screen** requires six paid supervised closed files and Ruth’s signed accuracy and privacy report before live use.
His **job search** depends on lost hours and a posted written bill-covering offer, while current pay lasts only while assigned.

steps.text: Ask association for paid review and named sign-off rules
Learn parts-audit on six closed files in approved paid time; use live after Ruth-signed six-error/privacy clearance
If refused, study free examples while assigned paid files remain
If hours fall, seek posted utility-billing: written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start, Elise-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 would handle the garage tax thinking before hands-on robots come around 2031. A repair bay may have more time; our accounts desk does not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the association for dated pay and redundancy terms and tell clients to keep the repair orders during any handover. I would not promise that a new rule will arrive in time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my paid accounts work to end in the first year after AGI. Two weeks saved would be gone before the next rent, and Elise’s bakery pay cannot replace mine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would cancel our spare mobile contract when its term ends and put the released monthly fee into emergency cash. After job loss in 2028, I would apply for posted utility meter-billing work only with written wages covering rent and food, a fixed start and workable hours; I would take firm closeout work only while it remains paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed and I have already pictured the rent notice. I can make calls, but there are few similar accounting jobs here.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill can you stop now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The spare phone belongs to our grown son who has moved out, and he says he no longer uses it. I would confirm with him before the cancellation date and transfer only the fee we actually stop paying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would utility billing be safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Meter billing still uses screens and numbers, so AGI can touch it in 2028. I would treat a posted paid vacancy as a way to earn now, not a permanent shelter.

say: I would ask for **dated pay terms** as the garage accounts desk faces 2028 AGI.
I would keep **repair orders** available for clients during handover.
think: I expect my **accounts wage** to end after 2028.
Two weeks saved and Elise’s wage cannot cover the **next rent**.
do: Cancel the **spare mobile** at term end after checking with our son; save only the released monthly fee.
After job loss, seek **posted meter billing** with written rent-and-food-covering pay, fixed start and workable hours; take closeout only while paid.
feel: **Alarmed** about likely wage loss and the next rent.
S2.quote: The spare phone belongs to our grown son who has moved out, and he says he no longer uses it.
fieldNote: The **mobile cancellation** releases a recurring fee after confirmation with his son; current savings are not relabelled as new income.
Meter billing’s **screen work** faces AGI at 2028, so he treats a posted vacancy as income, not safety.

steps.text: Cancel spare mobile at term end after checking with son; save released fee
Take paid firm closeout files only while offered
After 2028 loss, seek posted meter-billing: written pay covering rent and food, fixed start, workable hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years before 2031 would let me learn how to challenge a wrong tax assessment, but the accounts desk still changes in 2031. The robots in 2034 do not buy us extra tax seasons.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the association to ask for funded paid places on the appeals rota. The people who check routine files need a fair chance to learn that work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may keep some paid client dispute work, but I cannot assume the firm will have enough of it after AGI. At 63, I still need actual wages unless we can show bills are covered another way.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Ruth for one paid supervised tax appeal each quarter, completing the assigned cases with senior adviser Nadia if approved. If refused, I will read free published appeal decisions while keeping paid garage returns only while the firm offers them, including after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my future wage, but five years gives me time to practise carefully. I would not spend our two week reserve on course fees.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a real appeal include?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A real tax appeal has a notice, repair invoices and a deadline. My senior adviser Nadia would check my draft before it goes out; I want to learn on an assigned case, not a video.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if paid disputes end?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If paid disputes end after 2031 and we still need my wage, I will seek posted utility billing only with written pay covering rent, confirmed start and shifts fitting Elise’s bakery work. I will not leave current paid files for a possible opening.

say: I would ask for **funded appeal places** through the association.
I would set **2031** as the desk deadline, before robots.
think: I cannot assume **paid disputes** survive AGI.
Our **two week reserve** cannot fund a course or a long job gap.
do: Complete one **paid supervised appeal** quarterly only if Ruth assigns Nadia; otherwise study free decisions while paid files last.
After 2031 dispute loss, seek **posted utility billing** only if wage needed, with written rent covering pay, start and Elise-compatible shifts.
feel: **Anxious** about future earnings, with time for supervised practice.
S3.quote: A real tax appeal has a notice, repair invoices and a deadline.
fieldNote: The **quarterly appeal** is actual assigned paid practice with Nadia’s supervision and Ruth’s approval.
The **free-case fallback** and current garage pay persist only while the firm assigns files; outside work requires posted written terms.

steps.text: Ask association for funded paid appeal places
Complete quarterly Nadia-supervised appeal only if Ruth assigns paid time
Otherwise read free decisions while assigned paid garage returns remain after 2031
Seek posted utility job after loss if needed, with written rent-covering pay, confirmed start, Elise-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 makes me 68, and Elise and I would like to choose our working days then. The desk still meets AGI in 2036, three years before robots reach the repair bay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the association each year how many paid garage reviews the firm expects to keep. I would tell younger staff that a forecast must include wages, not only software speed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I cannot say today whether we will have enough confirmed income to stop work at 68. Two weeks saved now is a small cushion, and I will not ask our grown son to stand in for a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns while offered and transfer twelve from each monthly wage into emergency cash if rent and food allow. After 2036, only if the bills still need my wage and the firm cuts paid hours, I would apply for posted utility records work with written pay covering the gap, confirmed start and workable shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious even with a decade because our current margin is so thin. I would feel alarmed if the firm stopped paying and we still lacked enough income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would the extra cash come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Twelve comes from a real monthly wage, not the two weeks already saved. I would pause it when Elise’s bakery shifts fall or rent rises.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show another employer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the notebook of corrected garage parts and show it when asking for paid work, but I would not call it a guaranteed job. The utility office would still have to advertise a place.

say: I would ask for **paid review forecasts** through the association.
I would tell juniors to ask about **wages**, not only speed.
think: I cannot plan on **unconfirmed later income** at 68.
Our current **two week reserve** keeps the future fragile.
do: Keep **assigned paid returns** only while offered and save twelve monthly from wages if rent and food permit.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted utility records** only if income still short, with written gap-covering pay, start and shifts.
Ask the **staff association** each year for paid garage-review forecasts.
feel: **Anxious** because current cash is thin despite the long runway.
S4.quote: I would keep the notebook of corrected garage parts and show it when asking for paid work, but I would not call it a guaranteed job.
fieldNote: The **twelve monthly** is new wage cash, stopped if Elise’s shifts fall or rent rises; no pension is assumed.
The **post-2036 search** requires actual household need, reduced paid hours, a posted vacancy and written wages.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid garage returns only while offered
Save twelve monthly from wages if rent and food allow; pause if Elise’s hours fall
After 2036 cuts, seek posted utility job only if gap; require written gap-covering pay/start/shifts
Ask staff association annually for paid garage-review forecasts

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because our garage accounts desk could stop paying before I find another wage. Written last-shift dates, paid appeals practice and a real posted utility job would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask why I keep the old repair orders. A starter motor entered twice can take the rent money out of a garage owner’s pocket.

headlineQuote: A starter motor entered twice can take the rent money out of a garage owner’s pocket.
portrait: Colin is a **58 year old experienced** accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification who prepares garage accounts and returns.
He uses **AI daily** for parts sorting but calls clients when a repair order contradicts the screen.
Lower pay, Elise’s bakery wage, grown children, **two weeks saved** and few local firms make even a plateau anxious.
He presses for **paid review time** and supervised appeals, while keeping job moves conditional on posted written wages.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could end his paid garage accounts before another wage begins.
whatWouldHelp: **Written shift dates**, paid appeal practice and a posted utility job would help.
